fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Pilate asks Jesus straight out, "Are You the King of the Jews?" and Jesus replies, "You have said so…" (Mark 15:2) That is not a no. Jesus doesn't tell Pilate He isn't.

Yes, baker. "…the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom." (Mark 15:8) That custom was to release a prisoner of their choosing at the feast (Mark 15:6). The crowd is asking him to do what he always does. That's the ask.

Not quite, friend. Mark says the chief priests "…stirred up the crowd…" (Mark 15:11) It doesn't say they warned anybody. The text tells us what the chief priests did, and the goal was to have Barabbas released instead.

Yes, baker. "And they shouted back, 'Crucify Him!'" (Mark 15:13) Pilate had asked what to do with the One they call the King of the Jews. That's the crowd's answer. I think this is a heavy moment, so let's let it be heavy.

Right, baker. Pilate asks, "Why? What evil has He done?" and gets no quiet at all. "They shouted all the louder, 'Crucify Him!'" (Mark 15:14) The crowd's answer got louder, and it's the same two words again.

That's it, baker. "They began to salute Him: 'Hail, King of the Jews!'" (Mark 15:18) Pilate had used the title King of the Jews when he questioned Jesus (Mark 15:2). Here the soldiers use it in their salute, along with the robe and the crown.

Right, baker. "After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him." (Mark 15:20) The robe comes off and His own clothes go back on. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
